rationale: PINS qualified_calls OWNERSHIP across nested scopes (M3). The payload walk used to stop at every nested function, so a callback's call was absent from the payload while the graph carried the edge, and the javascript twin disagreed. The rule pinned here: a call belongs to the symbol that lexically owns it — the nearest enclosing SYMBOL, not the symbol the walk started from. (1) a callback with no symbol keeps the enclosing symbol's payload; (2) a nested `function inner(){}` IS a symbol, so its call must NOT appear on the enclosing symbol — the anti-pollution direction, which an includes-only check cannot catch; (3) an object-literal method is its own symbol too (TSD7), so the call inside it belongs to the method, and the payload pin and the calls-edge pin must agree on that; (4) the payload is a SET of paths, not a multiset; (5) two same-named methods on different classes must not share a payload. The calls EDGES are pinned alongside so the payload can never be read as 'the graph', only as its per-symbol projection.
